title: neutralizeText lets join passcodes/passwords and meeting identifiers through in several common forms; the title reaches alert title and body
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/attention-alerts.ts:46-49 (SECRETISH requires `<word>\s*[=:]` directly after the word; URLISH requires a scheme; no handling of percent-encoding, zero-width chars, newline-split values)
evidence: buildAttentionAlerts with one skipped overlap-lost item, title = X; resulting alert.title/body text: X='Meeting ID: 987 6543 2100 Passcode 778899' -> unchanged (leaks id+passcode); 'Meeting ID 987 6543 2100 pwd abc123' -> unchanged; 'pwd abc123XYZ' -> unchanged; 'meetingPassword=Sekret9' -> unchanged; '"passcode":"Q123"' -> unchanged; 'pass\u200bcode=ZWS1' -> unchanged (U+200B/200D/2060/180E/00AD/FE0F are not stripped, so zero-width splits evade the match); 'https://zoom.us/j/1?pwd=\nSPLIT' -> 'link SPLIT' (value after the newline); 'https%3A%2F%2Fzoom.us%2Fj%2F1%3Fpwd%3DPCT' -> unchanged; 'zoom.us%2Fj%2F1%3Fpwd%3DPCT2' -> unchanged; 'zoom.us/j/123?pwd=abc' -> 'zoom.us/j/123?secret' (scheme-less host keeps meeting id and path; a scheme-less registrant path is kept whole); full-width 'ｈｔｔｐｓ：／／zoom.us/j/1?pwd=FW' and 'https:\u2215\u2215zoom.us\u2215j\u22151?pwd=LOOK' keep host and path; 'Dial in +1 555 123 4567 PIN 889900#' -> PIN and phone kept; 'key sk-ant-api03-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' and 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE' kept; 'bob(at)evil.example' kept. Spec: no secret/link/third-party personal data may reach an alert.
fix_direction: Normalise first (NFKC, strip all format/zero-width/soft-hyphen chars), percent-decode once, then redact: pwd|passcode|password|passwd|pin|token|tk|code|secret|key followed by optional quote/space/=/: and a value; scheme-less host/path patterns; digit groups of 6+ (with spaces); long base64/hex-like words; phone patterns. Or stronger: do not echo free-text titles, only an allow-shaped prefix. This evidence list is the regression floor.

title: sessionKey (skipped item key or job-map key) is copied verbatim into AttentionAlert.sessionKey and, only character-mapped, into the dedupe key, so a URL/email/newline in it reaches the output
evidence: skipped sessionKey='cal:x https://zoom.us/j/1?pwd=SKEY bob@evil.example\nACTION' -> alert.sessionKey identical (raw, with newline) and key='attn:overlap-lost:cal:x_https:__zoom.us_j_1_pwd_SKEY_bob_evil.example_ACTION'. Same for a job-map key. Real sessionKeys today are cal:<id>, gmail:<id>, webinar-<hash>, so exposure depends on the wiring, but the module validates nothing.
fix_direction: Accept only /^[A-Za-z0-9:._-]{1,120}$/ session keys, else count in ignored as 'malformed-session-key'.

title: time zone label is run through neutralizeText, which strips underscores, so the printed zone is wrong for multi-word IANA zones
evidence: renderStart('2026-03-08T07:30:00Z','America/New_York') -> '2026-03-08 03:30 (America/NewYork)'; same for America/Los_Angeles, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires. The time is right, the label is not a real zone. Also renderStart('2026-10-10T19:00:00Z', undefined) -> '2026-10-10 19:00 ((untitled))' (formats in the machine zone but labels it '(untitled)'); buildAttentionAlerts guards non-string zones so only direct callers hit this.
fix_direction: The zone is already validated by Intl; print it verbatim and treat non-string as UTC before the Intl call.

title: dedupe key collisions: keyPart maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9:._|-] to _ and truncates at 160, so distinct situations share a key and the second alert is suppressed
evidence: skipped sessionKeys 'cal:a b', 'cal:a/b', 'cal:a_b' (all overlap-lost) -> all three key 'attn:overlap-lost:cal:a_b'; selectNewAlerts(alerts, []).fresh.length === 1. Two keys sharing a 200-char prefix and differing at char 201 -> identical key. Real Google ids are alphanumeric, so impact depends on wiring.
fix_direction: Reject non-conforming session keys (see 002) or append a short hash of the raw sessionKey when the mapping changed it.

title: test gaps on a text-sanitising module: control-character stripping, zero-width, key collisions, over-bound retention behaviour and underscore zones are unasserted
evidence: Mutation M2 (delete the control-character replace) SURVIVED: 10/10 tests pass (the later whitespace collapse hides it for \n, but NUL, U+0085 etc. stay unchecked). The ISS-R1ALERTS-001 forms and the 004 collision have no test. 9 other mutations were killed (URL replace, unknown-reason echo, timestamp in key, retention bound, UTC label, pwd/token pair, email, markup strip, bidi strip).
fix_direction: Add the ISS-R1ALERTS-001 corpus verbatim, a NUL/U+0085 title, an underscore zone, key-collision and >maxKeys cases.

title: the secret-keyword mask hides only ONE token after the keyword, so multi-word passcodes and passcodes of several short groups leak; synonyms and Hindi keywords are not in the list
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/alert-text.ts KEYWORDS / TAIL (`\S+` after the keyword) and DIGIT_GROUP threshold (6 digits total or a run of 3)
evidence: sanitize(X) -> output (all verbatim, title field of a skipped overlap-lost item): 'passcode: tiger seven blue' -> 'passcode (hidden) seven blue' (leaks 'seven blue'); 'password is correct horse battery staple' -> 'password (hidden) horse battery staple'; 'passphrase tiger seven blue' -> 'passphrase (hidden) seven blue'; 'code abc def ghi' -> 'code (hidden) def ghi'; 'secret word: banana' -> 'secret (hidden) banana'; 'meeting password tiger blue' -> 'meeting password (hidden) blue'; 'zoom password: aB3 xY' -> 'zoom password (hidden) xY'; 'PASS CODE: 12 34' -> 'PASS CODE (hidden) 34'; 'passcode 12 34' -> 'passcode (hidden) 34'; 'pin 4 2 1 7' -> 'pin (hidden) 2 1 7'; 'OTP 42 17' -> 'OTP (hidden) 17'; 'PIN is 7 3' -> 'PIN (hidden) 3'. Keywords not recognised, value kept: 'Pass: 42 17', 'pw 42 17', 'pw: tiger', 'pass 42', 'psw tiger', 'pswd 42', 'passkey tiger', 'login: tiger', 'kood 12', 'kód 42', 'mot de passe tiger', 'contraseña tiger', and Hindi 'पासकोड: 12', 'पिन 42', 'पासवर्ड tiger seven', 'कोड tiger', 'paasvard tiger'. Spaced keyword 'p i n 42' and 'P.I.N. 42' -> unchanged. Digit groups under 6 total across separators with no run of 3: '1 2 3 4 5', '12 34 5', '12.34.5' kept. Non-ASCII digits ARE masked (१२३४५६, ١٢٣٤٥٦, mixed 12३४56 -> (hidden)); the gap is the one-token reach.
fix_direction: After a secret keyword mask the whole remainder of the clause (to end of title or the next sentence-ending punctuation), not one token; add synonyms (pw, psw, pswd, passwrd, passkey, access/joining/meeting/security/verification code, login, kood/kod/kód, mot de passe, contraseña) and Hindi/Devanagari forms (पासकोड, पासवर्ड, पिन, कोड, ओटीपी) as keywords; treat any number of 1-2 digit groups separated by spaces/dots/hyphens after a keyword as the value; count total digits >=4 within a spaced group after any keyword. Replay this row verbatim as part of the regression floor (D-015).

title: mutation survives: removing the fixed-point repeat in sanitize() passes all 30 tests, so no test shows that a character removed by the allowlist can join text into something maskable
evidence: Mutation `if (t === s) return t;` -> `return t;` (single pass): alert-text.test.ts + attention-alerts.test.ts 30/30 pass. Real code: sanitize('12_34_56') is '(hidden)' only because round 2 sees '123456' after the allowlist strips '_'; a single pass would print '123456'. Verified: one mask+allowlist pass on '12_34_56' yields '123456'; on '12[]34' yields '1234'.
fix_direction: Add tests whose secret exists only after the allowlist removes a character: '12_34_56', '12[]34', 'pass_x_code tiger' style joins, and assert each.

title: AttentionAlert.startTime echoes the caller's raw string whenever Date.parse accepts it; V8's legacy parser ignores parenthesised text, so free text rides along
area: packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/attention-alerts.ts startOf() and the job-row `startTime` read; `...(startTime ? { startTime } : {})`
evidence: startTimes {'cal:a': 'Mon Oct 12 2026 (pwd=Sekret9 https://zoom.us/j/1) 10:00'} (Date.parse is finite) -> alert.startTime === that exact string (body 'Starts:' line is correctly formatted from the parsed instant). Same for a job row `startTime`. '2026-10-12T10:00:00Z (passcode tiger seven)' is rejected by Date.parse (not echoed).
fix_direction: Store `new Date(ms).toISOString()` instead of the caller's string.

title: residual class a deny-list cannot close: a secret with no recognised keyword and no digit/shape pattern is echoed (for example 'Webinar tiger')
evidence: sanitize('Webinar tiger') === 'Webinar tiger'. Also open: keywords in languages not on the list (Russian, Arabic, Chinese...), leetspeak (p4ss, c0de), interior punctuation other than space . - _ (for example p/i/n), confusable letters from scripts other than Cyrillic/Greek (Armenian, Cherokee), and digit groups of 4 or fewer digits with no keyword ('1 2 3 4').
fix_direction: Not closable by listing words. The only complete fix is to stop echoing free text: send the alert with the event id, case, start time and a non-sensitive identifier supplied by the wiring (organiser display name, calendar name), or show the title only to the owner after authentication. Decision for Umesh: accept the residual (operator chat is trusted, titles come from invitations) or drop the title from alerts.
